title: Search Insert Position
statement: Given a sorted list of distinct integers and a target, return the index of the target if present; otherwise return the index where it would have to be inserted to keep the list sorted.

hints.1_question: Instead of searching for equality, what question does each probe answer about where the target belongs?
hints.2_nudge: You want the first index whose value is >= target. If nums[mid] < target the answer is to the right of mid; otherwise mid could be the answer.
hints.3_big_hint: lo, hi = 0, len(nums). While lo < hi: mid; if nums[mid] < target: lo = mid+1 else hi = mid. Return lo. Note hi starts at len(nums), not len-1.

known_bugs.name: returns -1 when the target is absent
known_bugs.followup: The problem asks for where the target would be inserted. What does your function return when it isn't found?

known_bugs.name: can never return len(nums)
known_bugs.followup: If the target is bigger than everything, what is the largest index your search can ever return?

known_bugs.name: lo = mid never makes progress
known_bugs.followup: When lo and hi are adjacent and nums[mid] < target, what are lo and mid, and does the range shrink?

followups: Why is `hi = len(nums)` instead of `len(nums) - 1` right for this problem?
How does this change if duplicates are allowed and you want the first or last position?
